slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Look at the two segments in the figure. Most people say the one with the outward fins is longer. Measure them: they are exactly the same length.

Our eyes are good at noticing patterns but easy to fool. Geometry asks a sharper question: not "does it look true?" but "can we show that it must be true?" A conjecture is a statement we think is true. It becomes a theorem only when we prove it from facts we have already accepted.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: A drawing shows two angles that look equal. Is that enough to say they are equal?
slides.reveal: No. A drawing can suggest a conjecture, but only measurement within a stated error or, better, a proof can settle it. In geometry we prove it.
